name: Business Manager
intro: You will peek at the example business (Miller Plumbing), then set the app up for a pretend builder, Miller Construction, using the General Construction price list. You add a customer (Linda Hansen), price a garage-framing job, mark it approved, take a deposit, record a lumber bill, add to-dos and tax dates, and check everything is still there after a reload. Never press a 📨 Send, 📞 Call or 💬 Message button — they would open your real texts or email.

steps.do: When the app opens, a “Welcome to Business Manager” card is at the bottom. Tap the small link “skip the tour” at its bottom-right.
steps.see: The card asks “How do you want to start?” with “🧪 Keep the examples to play with” (it mentions Miller Plumbing) and “✨ Start fresh with my own”.
steps.tip: A green greeting may show at the top for a few seconds — it goes away by itself. A purple “Test copy” pill means you are in a safe test copy.

steps.do: Tap “🧪 Keep the examples to play with”.
steps.see: An example business opens: “Miller Plumbing & Repair” at the top, a note “This is an example business. Play with anything.”, “Good afternoon, Dan.” (or morning/evening), Owed to me $175, Paid this month $5,035, and a “NEEDS YOU (6)” list that starts “Mike Peterson — $175.00 is 6 days late”.
steps.tip: Look around if you like, but do not press “Remind”, “Send” or “Check in” — they open a text message.

steps.do: Scroll to the top and tap “Start my own business” in the example note. On the next screen, tap “Next →” without typing anything.
steps.see: A “Set up · about two minutes” chat asks “First: what’s your business called, and what’s your name?” with two boxes. Tapping Next with them empty shows a box: “What’s the business called? (Your own name is fine.)” — tap OK and you stay on the question.

steps.do: Type the business name in the first box and your name in the second box (both below), then tap “Next →”.
steps.see: It asks “What do you need, Dave?” with “🧾 Just quotes (Quick Quote)” and “🧰 The whole business” — the second one already shows “✓ Picked”.

steps.do: Tap “🧰 The whole business”.
steps.see: “Good to meet you, Dave. What kind of work do you do?” with 12 buttons, including “🏗️ General Construction”.

steps.do: Tap “🏗️ General Construction”.
steps.see: “How should customers reach you? This goes on your estimates and invoices.” with Phone, Email and Business address (optional).

steps.do: Type the phone and email below into the first two boxes and tap “Next →”.
steps.see: Your answer shows as a bubble, and the next question is “Before you start a job, do customers usually get a price in writing?” with three answers.

steps.do: Instead of answering the rest, tap “Skip — turn everything on” at the bottom-right. Read the list, then tap “Let’s go →”.
steps.see: “All set, Dave. Here’s what I turned on for you:” — Estimates, Itemized prices, Deposits & progress billing, Schedule, Job costs, Crew & hours, Expenses & profit, To-do & due dates, Invoices with a Pay now link — and “I started your price list with typical general construction prices.” After Let’s go: “Miller Construction” at the top, “Good afternoon, Dave.”, Owed to me $0 and “✅ All caught up. Nice work.”
steps.tip: A short tip “Tip: tap + to add your first job” shows at the bottom for a moment.

steps.do: Tap ⚙️ More (bottom-right), then “🏷 Price list” (it says 9 items).
steps.see: Nine rows with a price each: Project supervision (per day) 650, Labor crew (per hour) 85, Framing (per sq ft) 9, Concrete (per cu yd) 240, Drywall (per sq ft) 3.5, Permit & inspection fees 0, Materials (at cost) 0, Dumpster / haul-away 550, Equipment rental (per day) 325.
steps.tip: The item names are cut off on a small phone — tap a name box and move along it to read the rest.

steps.do: In the Framing row, change the price 9 to the number below, then tap on the empty area above the list.
steps.see: A green “Saved ✓” pill shows briefly. The Framing row now says 10.

steps.do: Tap the round yellow “+ New” at the bottom, then “👤 New customer”. Type the name, phone and address below (leave Email empty) and tap “Save customer”.
steps.type: Linda Hansen · 847-555-0142 · 1420 Ridge Rd, Gurnee, IL
steps.see: Linda Hansen’s page: her phone and address, buttons 📞 Call, 💬 Message, 📍 Map, “Paid you, all time $0.00”, “No jobs yet.” and “➕ New job for Linda”.
steps.tip: Do not press Call or Message — they open your real phone.

steps.do: Tap “➕ New job for Linda”. The Customer box already says Linda Hansen. In “What’s the job?” type the first part below, in Details type the second part, then tap “Save job →”.
steps.type: Garage framing · 20x20 detached garage. Frame walls and roof, about 400 sq ft.
steps.see: The job page: “Garage framing” with “#1001 · Linda Hansen”, a “New” label, your details, and under PRICE / ESTIMATE “No price yet.” with “⚡ Draft from my price list”, “➕ Add item” and Total $0.00.
steps.tip: Do not press “📨 Send the estimate” or “📨 Send estimate”.

steps.do: Tap “⚡ Draft from my price list”.
steps.see: Two lines appear, each marked “📌 price list”: Framing (per sq ft) $10.00 and Drywall hang & finish (per sq ft) $3.50. Total $13.50. Note: the draft puts 1 of each — it does not pick up the “400 sq ft” from your details, and it added drywall you did not ask for.

steps.do: Tap the Drywall line and tap “Remove”. Then tap the Framing line, change “How many” to the number below and tap “Save”. Then tap “➕ Add item”, tap “Dumpster / haul-away $550.00” and tap “Save”.
steps.see: Framing shows “400 × $10.00” and $4,000.00; Dumpster / haul-away shows $550.00; Total $4,550.00.

steps.do: Scroll down a little and tap “👍 They said yes”. The box already says Linda Hansen and today’s date — tap “Mark approved”.
steps.see: A note “Approved. Next: pick a day.”, the label at the top now says Approved, and the estimate shows “✅ Approved by Linda Hansen on” today’s date.

steps.do: Scroll down to BILLING (Job total $4,550.00) and tap “Deposit (30%)”.
steps.see: “Invoice #2001” for Linda Hansen: $1,365.00, “still owed · Deposit”, “Not sent”, and one line “Deposit — 30% of Garage framing ($4,550.00)”.
steps.tip: Do not press “📨 Send invoice with pay link”.

steps.do: Tap “💵 Record a payment”. The amount already says 1365.00. Change “How” to Check and tap “Save payment”.
steps.see: A note “Deposit received 👍”; the invoice says “paid in full · Deposit”, Balance due $0.00, and under PAYMENTS: today, Check, $1,365.00.

steps.do: Tap 💵 Money at the bottom. Then tap “➕ Expense”, type the amount and the store below, choose the job “Garage framing — Linda Hansen” under “For a job?”, and tap “Save”.
steps.see: Before: Money in $1,365.00, Profit $1,365.00. As you type Menards the kind changes to “Materials & supplies” by itself. After saving: Money out −$1,200.00, Profit $165.00, “Set aside about $41 for income tax”, and under JOB BY JOB: Garage framing, $3,350, 74% kept.

steps.do: Tap 🏠 Today, then “📝 To-do”. Type the to-do below, pick a date 3 days from today, tap “Add”. Then tap “📋 Add common due dates — taxes, truck, insurance” and “Add the ticked ones”. Finally tap the round ○ next to the trusses to-do.
steps.type: Order roof trusses for Hansen garage
steps.see: First “THIS WEEK (1) · Order roof trusses for Hansen garage · Due in 3 days”. Then “Added 7 due dates”, including Payroll taxes (Form 941) Due Mon Nov 2, Quarterly estimated taxes (IRS 1040-ES) Due Fri Jan 15 and File income taxes (Schedule C) Due Thu Apr 15. Tapping ○ shows “Done ✓” and the trusses move to “DONE LATELY”.

steps.do: Pull the page down to reload. If a “What would you like to do?” page shows, tap “Pick up where I left off”. Tap 🏠 Today, then 🧰 Jobs.
steps.see: Everything is kept: Today shows “Miller Construction”, Paid this month $1,365; Jobs shows “Garage framing · Linda Hansen · $4,550 · Approved”, and the to-do list still has the tax dates.
